name: Occupational Therapy Assistant
description: Occupational therapy assistants deliver the treatment that gets people back to doing ordinary things — dressing, cooking, writing, working, playing — after injury, stroke, developmental delay or mental illness. ⚠ A median of $72,300 on a two-year degree, growing 21%. ⚠⚠⚠ And the finding worth acting on: it pays MORE and grows FASTER than the physical therapist assistant, and Florida trains a QUARTER as many. Four institutions, 57 graduates a year. This page covers the assistant, the aide and the therapist.
credentialNote: ⚠ Florida licenses occupational therapy assistants under Chapter 468, Part III, and the route is short and clearly defined. You need an associate degree from an ACCREDITED occupational therapy assistant programme, **24 weeks of supervised fieldwork**, and a pass in the examination approved by the National Board for Certification in Occupational Therapy — which yields the COTA credential. ⚠⚠ Fees are modest: $100 application, $75 initial licence and a $5 unlicensed-activity fee, $180 in total. Electronic fingerprinting is required following Florida's HB 975 in 2024, with a $43.25 FDLE retention fee at renewal. ⚠ Renewal takes 26 hours of continuing education every two years — 22 general hours of which at least 14 must be live and no more than 12 by home study, plus 2 hours on prevention of medical errors and 2 on Florida laws and rules. ⚠⚠⚠ Note the contrast with the AIDE, which this page also covers: occupational therapy aides are typically NOT regulated by state law, need only a high school diploma, and earn $39,160 against the assistant's $72,300. The licence is the whole difference.
bodyHtml:
Three roles, and the licence is what separates them

RoleSOC2025 medianJobsOutlook 2025–35Entry
Occupational therapy aide31-2012⚠ $39,1604,400⚠ 4%high school, unregulated
Occupational therapy assistant31-2011$72,30052,200✅✅ 21%accredited associate + licence
Occupational therapist29-1122the professional tier——⚠ master's or doctorate

⚠⚠⚠ $33,140 and seventeen percentage points of growth separate the aide from the assistant, and the thing in between is a two-year accredited degree and a licence. The aide role is not a stepping stone in any formal sense — it is a different, unregulated job — but it is a legitimate way to see the work before committing.

✅ 21% growth on 52,200 jobs, with about 8,600 openings a year across assistants and aides, is one of the strongest outlooks on this site.

⚠⚠⚠ The comparison that should decide this for some readers

This site already carries the physical therapist assistant path. Put the two side by side and the result is counter-intuitive.

Occupational therapy assistantPhysical therapist assistant
2025 median✅ $72,300$68,380
Growth 2025–35✅ 21%17%
Florida institutions⚠⚠ 417
Florida graduates a year⚠⚠ 57267

⚠⚠ The better-paid, faster-growing credential is the one Florida trains a quarter as many people for. That is not a market signal about quality — it is a supply fact, and it works in the graduate's favour. The catch is geography: with four programmes in the state — Daytona State, FSCJ, Polk State and State College of Florida–Manatee-Sarasota — where you live may simply decide this.

⚠ So the honest advice is: if either appeals and you can reach an occupational therapy assistant programme, look hard at it before defaulting to the physical therapist assistant just because it is nearer.

What the work actually is, and how it differs from physical therapy

O*NET, on occupational therapy assistants: instruct, or assist in instructing, patients and families in home programs, basic living skills; monitor patients' performance in therapy activities, providing encouragement; observe and record patients' progress, attitudes, and behavior and maintain this information in client records.

⚠⚠ The distinction students get wrong: physical therapy works on MOVEMENT, occupational therapy works on FUNCTION. A physical therapist assistant might work on restoring shoulder range of motion; an occupational therapy assistant works on whether the person can now get dressed, and if not, what adaptation or technique makes it possible. That takes the profession into places physical therapy does not go — paediatric developmental work, mental health, cognitive rehabilitation, hand therapy, home and workplace adaptation, and assistive technology.

⚠ It is also less uniformly physical. Transfers and lifting are still part of it, but a larger share of the caseload is fine motor, cognitive and behavioural — which suits a different person than the sports-and-orthopaedics image of rehabilitation.

⚠⚠ The professional tier is shorter here than in physical therapy

If the therapist role is the eventual goal, occupational therapy is currently the shorter route. Florida's 4 professional programmes produced 62 master's degrees and 47 professional doctorates — FIU 47 master's, UF 47 doctorates, FAMU 15 master's. Physical therapy, by contrast, is 100% doctoral in Florida: all 350 credentials are the DPT.

⚠⚠⚠ But the same warning applies as on the physical therapy path: the assistant associate degree is NOT advanced standing toward the therapist qualification. An assistant who wants to become an occupational therapist completes a bachelor's and then applies to a master's or doctoral programme in open competition. Choose the level deliberately rather than treating the assistant degree as a first instalment.

⚠ The fieldwork is the part that structures your life

Florida requires 24 weeks of supervised fieldwork for the assistant licence. That is close to half a year of full-time placement, on the facility's schedule and often not near your home.

⚠⚠ Ask each of the four programmes where its fieldwork placements are and how they are allocated, because with so few programmes the sites are spread widely, and this is the part of the course that cannot be fitted around a job. Expect background screening, immunisations and current CPR to be complete before it starts.

Necessary skills

  • Activity analysis. Breaking “make a cup of tea” into the components a person can and cannot do is the intellectual core of the profession.
  • Creativity with adaptation. The answer is often a modified tool, a different technique or a changed environment rather than more exercise.
  • Fine motor and cognitive assessment, which is where this differs most from physical therapy.
  • Patience with slow, functional goals that matter enormously to the person and look small on paper.
  • Documentation. Your notes justify continued treatment to the insurer and the therapist's plan of care depends on them.
  • Working across settings — schools, hospitals, skilled nursing, mental health and the home — which is broader than most allied health roles.

Advice

⚠⚠ Check all four Florida programmes, not just the nearest. With 57 graduates a year statewide, geography is the binding constraint, and it is worth knowing whether any of Daytona State, FSCJ, Polk State or State College of Florida is reachable before settling for a different career.

⚠ Verify ACOTE accreditation directly. Florida's licence requires graduation from an accredited programme and the NBCOT examination requires it too — so the accreditation is what makes the whole route work.

⚠ Do not assume the assistant degree leads on to the therapist qualification. It does not, in the same way the physical therapist assistant degree does not. If the therapist role is the goal, look at whether going straight for a bachelor's and then the master's is the better plan — and note that occupational therapy still has a master's route where physical therapy no longer does.

And spend time in a paediatric setting and a skilled nursing facility before choosing. They are both occupational therapy and they are barely the same work — one is children's development and play, the other is helping frail adults keep their independence — and most applicants have only pictured one of them.

cipCodes.note: Rehabilitation and therapeutic professions — the professional tier this path sits beneath, covering occupational therapy's own master's and doctoral programmes as well as physical therapy's. ⚠ Included so the reader can see the level above, but note the assistant degree is not advanced standing toward it.

⚠ Psychology — 10 Florida public institutions and 6,549 credentials. A genuine feeder, because a large part of occupational therapy is cognitive, developmental and mental-health work, and psychology graduates are common applicants to the professional programmes.
Kinesiology and exercise science — 16 Florida public institutions. The common undergraduate route for students who decide on a rehabilitation profession during a bachelor's rather than before one.

programs.note: The programme itself — ⚠ only 4 Florida public institutions award the assistant degree, producing 57 graduates a year. Read its degrees note before assuming the nearest rehabilitation programme is the right one: this credential pays more and grows faster than its physical therapy equivalent and is far harder to find.

⚠ Not a route — separate licences, separate accreditation, no transfer between the assistant credentials. ⚠⚠ Named because it is the choice every applicant is really making, and the comparison is counter-intuitive: physical therapy is at 17 Florida institutions against 4, but its assistant role pays $68,380 against $72,300 and grows 17% against 21%.

⚠ Not a route. Named as the third rehabilitation profession working the same caseloads in schools, hospitals and skilled nursing. ⚠⚠ Its assistant tier needs a BACHELOR'S plus specified coursework, where this one needs a two-year associate degree — which makes occupational therapy the more accessible of the two.

courses.reason: Anatomy and Physiology I — 20 institutions. The structural foundation, required with a grade of C or higher by Florida occupational therapy assistant programmes and the course competitive admission turns on.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Two equivalent packagings: BSC2085 plus BSC2085L at 20 institutions, the combined BSC2085C at 7. Where split, take both halves in the same term.

courses.reason: Anatomy and Physiology I Laboratory — 19 institutions, the corequisite half.
Anatomy and Physiology II — 19 institutions. Neurological and systemic content, which matters here because so much of the caseload is stroke, brain injury and developmental.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Also carried as the combined BSC2086C at 7 institutions.

courses.reason: Anatomy and Physiology II Laboratory — 19 institutions.

Introduction to Psychology — 33 institutions. ⚠⚠ More central here than in physical therapy: mental health, cognition and behaviour are a substantial part of occupational therapy practice, not an adjacent concern.
Human Growth and Development — 29 institutions. Paediatric occupational therapy is one of the largest practice areas, and developmental milestones are the framework the whole of it is built on.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Required by most Florida occupational therapy assistant programmes, and more load-bearing here than on the physical therapy side.

courses.reason: Nutrition — 21 institutions. Feeding and swallowing, meal preparation as an activity of daily living, and the nutritional side of recovery.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Check your programme's list — not universal, but common.

courses.reason: English Composition I — 39 institutions. Progress notes justify continued treatment to the insurer, and the therapist's plan of care is adjusted from what you wrote.
Interpersonal Communication — 16 institutions. Much of the work is persuading a discouraged person to attempt something difficult and undignified, and doing it well is the therapeutic skill.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Some colleges satisfy the same requirement with SPC1608 Public Speaking (16 institutions).

courses.reason: College Algebra — 36 institutions. The general-education mathematics most associate degrees require, and the one that travels if you later go on to a bachelor's and the professional tier.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ If the therapist qualification is a possibility, check the mathematics and statistics those programmes want before settling for the minimum.

courses.reason: Elementary Statistics — 39 institutions. Required by the professional programmes above this one, and the basis for reading the evidence behind an intervention.
